sentences: In a Joseon world where portraits were reserved for kings and scholar-officials, Shin Yun-bok painted an unnamed woman at nearly life size.
Her towering wig, short fitted jacket and billowing skirt reflect the height of fashion in late Joseon Seoul.
She tilts her head slightly and toys with the tassel ornament and ribbon of her jacket.
That small gesture brings time into a still image: hesitation, perhaps anticipation.
Beside the figure, the artist wrote that he had captured the spring stirring in her heart and conveyed her very spirit with his brush.
It is a quiet declaration that he painted a mind, not just a face.
